title_en: Fuzhou Commercial Building Preparatory Office v. Fujian Jiasheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan
ruling_gist_en: Bank interest, as income from the principal claim, constitutes statutory fruits. Unless otherwise specifically provided by law or specially agreed by the parties, the right to obtain the fruits transfers with the transfer of ownership of the principal thing.
keywords_en: Civil; dispute over loan contract; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Fujian Province; legal person; Contract Law; Security Law; effect of assignment of creditor's rights; calculation of interest; exercise of mortgage right; partial support; loan contract; assignment of creditor's rights; mortgage guarantee; statutory fruits transfer with the principal thing; loan dispute of Investment Development Co., Ltd.
full_text_en:
Fuzhou Commercial Building Preparatory Office v. Fujian Jiasheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan

【Ruling Summary】

Interest on bank loans, as proceeds from the principal claim, constitutes statutory fruits. Unless otherwise provided by law or specifically agreed by the parties, the right to obtain such fruits transfers with the transfer of ownership of the principal property.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 147

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Fuzhou Commercial Building Preparatory Office; domicile: No. 72 Xiangyuan Road, Fuzhou City, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Lin Zhiliang, General Manager of the Preparatory Office.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yunying, lawyer of Fujian Xinshitong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhou Junfang, lawyer of Fujian Xinshitong Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Fujian Jiasheng Investment Development Co., Ltd.; domicile: Room 723, Hot Spring Hotel, Wusi Road, Fuzhou City, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Naixiong, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Jinli, lawyer of Fujian Dazhong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Cheng Hao, lawyer of Fujian Dazhong Law Firm.

The appellant Fuzhou Commercial Building Preparatory Office (hereinafter referred to as the Preparatory Office), in dispute with the respondent Fujian Jiasheng Investment Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiasheng Company) over a loan, appealed against the civil judgment (2004) Min Min Chu Zi No. 67 rendered by the Fujian High People's Court to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of trial judge Xu Ruibai as presiding judge, acting trial judges Jia Wei and Sha Ling to hear the case. Court clerk Yuan Hongxia served as recorder. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found: On November 30, 1993, the Nanmen Sub-branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Fuzhou (hereinafter referred to as Nanmen ICBC) and the Preparatory Office entered into a maximum credit facility loan contract — the 1993 No. 93015 working capital loan contract. The contract stipulated: Nanmen ICBC would provide a maximum credit facility loan of RMB 60 million to the Preparatory Office, with a term from November 30, 1993 to December 27, 1998; the loan interest rate was 9.15‰ per month, and if the state adjusted the interest rate, the adjusted rate would apply. The actual disbursement and term of the loan would be evidenced by the loan receipt, and the special terms clearly provided that each loan disbursement would be subject to individual review. For overdue repayment, interest would be calculated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China. Fuzhou Mintian Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mintian Company), Fuzhou Taijiang Department Store (hereinafter referred to as Taijiang Department Store), and Fuzhou Rongfu Sugar, Wine and Non-staple Food Wholesale Company (hereinafter referred to as the Wholesale Company) acted as guarantors, providing joint and several liability guarantees for the Preparatory Office. After the execution of the above maximum credit facility loan contract, Nanmen ICBC disbursed five loans to the Preparatory Office. 1. On November 30, 1993, Nanmen ICBC disbursed a loan of RMB 10 million to the Preparatory Office, with a maturity date of June 27, 1995, for the construction of commercial outlets, at an interest rate of 9.15‰ per month. Mintian Company, Taijiang Department Store, and the Wholesale Company acted as guarantors, providing joint and several liability guarantees. After the loan was disbursed, the Preparatory Office failed to repay on time; subsequently, the loan was extended twice: the first extension from June 27, 1995 to June 27, 1996, at an interest rate of 10.98‰ per month; the second extension from June 27, 1996 to June 27, 1998, at an interest rate of 12.45‰ per month. Mintian Company, Taijiang Department Store, and the Wholesale Company continued to provide joint and several liability guarantees. However, after the extensions, the Preparatory Office still failed to repay. 2. On December 9, 1994, Nanmen ICBC and the Preparatory Office entered into the 94014 mortgage loan contract, disbursing a loan of RMB 15 million to the Preparatory Office, with a term from December 9, 1994 to December 13, 1996, for test piling and construction, at an interest rate of 10.98‰ per month, and if the state adjusted the interest rate, the adjusted rate would apply. For overdue repayment, interest would be calculated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China. The above loan was secured by a mortgage on the land use right of the Preparatory Office located on the east side of Bayiqi North Road, with a total area of 4,860 square meters (land certificate No.: Rong Zheng Di (1993) No. 137), and the mortgage was registered with the Fuzhou Land Administration Bureau, obtaining the land use right mortgage certificate Rong Di Zheng (1994) Zi No. 136. After the contract was signed, Nanmen ICBC disbursed the loan as agreed, but the Preparatory Office has not repaid it to date. 3. In November 1995, Nanmen ICBC and the Preparatory Office entered into the 95021 mortgage loan contract (i.e., Rong Fang Ya Zi No. 950098 mortgage loan contract for real estate under construction), disbursing a loan of RMB 7 million to the Preparatory Office. The loan term was from November 30, 1995 to November 23, 1997, for commercial outlet facilities, at an interest rate of 12.06‰ per month, and if the state adjusted the interest rate, the adjusted rate would apply. For overdue repayment, interest would be calculated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China. The above loan was secured by a mortgage on the total area of the building under construction located on the east side of Bayiqi North Road. The above mortgaged property was registered with the Fuzhou Real Estate Exchange Administration. After the mortgage loan contract was signed, Nanmen ICBC disbursed the loan of RMB 7 million as agreed, but the Preparatory Office has not repaid it to date. 4. On April 22, 1996, Nanmen ICBC and the Preparatory Office entered into the 96011 mortgage loan contract (i.e., Rong Fang Ya Zi No. 960064 mortgage loan contract for real estate under construction), disbursing a loan of RMB 1.5 million to the Preparatory Office, with a term from April 25, 1996 to April 3, 1998, for commercial outlet facilities, at an interest rate of 10.95‰ per month, and if the state adjusted the interest rate, the adjusted rate would apply. For overdue repayment, interest would be calculated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China. The above loan was secured by a mortgage on the total area of the building under construction located on the east side of Bayiqi North Road. The above mortgaged property was registered with the Fuzhou Real Estate Exchange Administration. After the mortgage loan contract was signed, Nanmen ICBC disbursed the loan of RMB 1.5 million as agreed, but the Preparatory Office has not repaid it to date. 5. On December 26, 1996, Nanmen ICBC and the Preparatory Office entered into loan contract No. 96040 for short-term RMB loans, disbursing a loan of RMB 2 million to the Preparatory Office. The loan term was from December 26, 1996 to December 26, 1997. The loan interest rate was 9.24‰ per month, and if the state adjusted the interest rate, the adjusted rate would apply. For overdue repayment, interest would be calculated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China. The above loan was guaranteed by Fuzhou Yifeng Group Company (hereinafter referred to as Yifeng Company) with joint and several liability. After the loan guarantee contract was signed, Nanmen ICBC disbursed the loan of RMB 2 million as agreed, but the Preparatory Office has not repaid it to date, and Yifeng Company also failed to perform its guarantee obligations.

On June 21, 2000, the Fujian Branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Fujian ICBC) and the Fuzhou Office of China Huarong Asset Management Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Huarong Fuzhou Office) entered into a Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement. Fujian ICBC assigned to Huarong Fuzhou Office all of the above five creditor's rights and their corresponding security rights held by Nanmen ICBC. The assignment of creditor's rights was notified to the Preparatory Office and the corresponding guarantors.

On June 26, 2003, Huarong Fuzhou Office and CITIC Trust & Investment Co., Ltd. entered into a Huarong Asset Disposal Property Trust Contract and Trust Property Disposal Entrustment Agreement, designating the above creditor's rights as trust property, but Huarong Fuzhou Office retained the right to dispose of the above property. During the period of managing the above creditor's rights, Huarong Fuzhou Office made multiple demands for payment to the Preparatory Office and the corresponding guarantors through newspaper announcements or mail delivery.

In November 2004, Huarong Fuzhou Office assigned all of the above five creditor's rights, which had been designated as trust property, to Jiasheng Company. The above assignment was jointly notified by CITIC Trust & Investment Co., Ltd. and Huarong Fuzhou Office to the Preparatory Office and the corresponding guarantors. To realize the creditor's rights, Jiasheng Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on November 26, 2004, requesting a judgment: ordering the Preparatory Office to repay the outstanding loan principal of RMB 35.5 million to Jiasheng Company, and to pay interest and penalty interest calculated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China until the date of actual repayment (interest and penalty interest temporarily calculated as of September 21, 2004, amounting to RMB 28,746,682.79); ordering that Jiasheng Company has priority right to be compensated from the proceeds of the mortgaged property used as security by the Preparatory Office (the land use right with a total area of 4,860 square meters located on the east side of Bayiqi North Road), to satisfy the creditor's rights held by Jiasheng Company under the 94014 mortgage loan contract (principal of RMB 15 million and corresponding interest and penalty interest); ordering that Jiasheng Company has priority right to be compensated from the proceeds of the mortgaged property used as security by the Preparatory Office (the building under construction located on the east side of Bayiqi North Road), to satisfy the creditor's rights held by Jiasheng Company under the mortgage loan contract for real estate under construction numbered Rong Fang Ya Zi No. 950098 (principal of RMB 7 million and corresponding interest and penalty interest); ordering that Jiasheng Company has priority right to be compensated from the proceeds of the mortgaged property used as security by the Preparatory Office (the building under construction located on the east side of Bayiqi North Road), to satisfy the creditor's rights held by Jiasheng Company under the mortgage loan contract for real estate under construction numbered Rong Fang Ya Zi No. 960064 (principal of RMB 1.5 million and corresponding interest and penalty interest); and ordering the Preparatory Office to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The court of first instance held: This case is a dispute arising from the assignment of creditor's rights. Jiasheng Company acquired the creditor's rights of loan principal of RMB 35.5 million and interest from Huarong Fuzhou Office on November 29, 2004. The assignment of creditor's rights and debts was lawful and valid. Jiasheng Company obtained lawful and valid creditor's rights, i.e., the loan principal of RMB 35.5 million and interest, including the above five loan contracts and three mortgage contracts. As for the creditor's rights of loan principal of RMB 35.5 million and interest of RMB 11,030,159.17 acquired by Huarong Fuzhou Office from Fujian ICBC on June 20, 2000, these were also lawful and valid. The interest generated on the principal of RMB 35.5 million from June 20, 2000 should belong to the new creditor, Huarong Fuzhou Office. In the assignment of creditor's rights in 2004, Huarong Fuzhou Office also transferred the interest after June 20, 2000 together with the principal to Jiasheng Company, explicitly stating that the interest generated after the assignment of the creditor's rights would also be transferred accordingly. Therefore, after acquiring the creditor's rights, Jiasheng Company also obtained the loan principal of RMB 35.5 million and interest of RMB 11,030,159.17, as well as the interest on the principal of RMB 35.5 million from June 20, 2000 until the time of the lawsuit. Regarding the issue of whether allocated land can be mortgaged, the court held that the Preparatory Office used its own land for mortgage. According to Article 45 of the Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Grant and Transfer of the Right to Use State-owned Land in Urban Areas, with the approval of the municipal or county people's government's land administration department and real estate administration department, the right to use allocated land and the ownership of buildings and other attachments on the land may be transferred, leased, or mortgaged. At the time of the loan, the Preparatory Office had obtained approval from the Fuzhou Land Administration Department and completed mortgage registration. Therefore, the mortgage contract and mortgage registration were lawful and valid. For the other two mortgage loan contracts for the building under construction, the mortgaged building under construction was also the Preparatory Office's own property and had been registered lawfully and validly with the relevant departments. Regarding the issue of whether the cases could be consolidated, according to the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the five loans in this case were of the same type and involved the same parties, so consolidation was in accordance with the law.

In summary, the court of first instance held: The creditor's rights assignment agreement between Jiasheng Company and Huarong Fuzhou Office was lawful and valid. The three mortgage loan contracts signed between the Preparatory Office and Nanmen ICBC were the true expressions of the parties' intentions and were lawful and valid. After the assignment of the creditor's rights, the mortgage contracts were also transferred to Jiasheng Company. According to the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, Jiasheng Company has the priority right to be compensated from the mortgaged land and the building under construction on the land. Therefore, Jiasheng Company's request for the Preparatory Office to repay the owed amount was in accordance with the law and should be supported. The Preparatory Office's defense lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported. Accordingly, the court of first instance, pursuant to Article 138 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 80, 82, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 33, 41, 46, and 56 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled: 1. The Preparatory Office shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, repay the outstanding loan principal of RMB 35.5 million and interest of RMB 11,030,159.17 to Jiasheng Company. Interest on the loan principal of RMB 35.5 million generated after the assignment of creditor's rights on June 21, 2000 shall be paid at 0.21‰ per day until the date of actual repayment. 2. Jiasheng Company has the priority right to be compensated from the proceeds of the mortgaged property used as security by the Preparatory Office (the land use right with a total area of 4,860 square meters located on the east side of Bayiqi North Road), to satisfy the creditor's rights held by Jiasheng Company under the 94014 mortgage loan contract (principal of RMB 15 million and corresponding interest and penalty interest). 3. Jiasheng Company has the priority right to be compensated from the proceeds of the mortgaged property used as security by the Preparatory Office (the building under construction located on the east side of Bayiqi North Road), to satisfy the creditor's rights held by Jiasheng Company under the mortgage loan contract for real estate under construction numbered Rong Fang Ya Zi No. 950098 (principal of RMB 7 million and corresponding interest and penalty interest). 4. Jiasheng Company has the priority right to be compensated from the proceeds of the mortgaged property used as security by the Preparatory Office (the building under construction located on the east side of Bayiqi North Road), to satisfy the creditor's rights held by Jiasheng Company under the mortgage loan contract for real estate under construction numbered Rong Fang Ya Zi No. 960064 (principal of RMB 1.5 million and corresponding interest and penalty interest). The first-instance acceptance fee of RMB 331,244 shall be borne by the Preparatory Office.

The Preparatory Office, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, claiming: The judgment of first instance was unclear in its findings of fact and improper in its application of law. 1. The judgment of first instance erroneously found the scope of the assignment of creditor's rights. In October 2000, the notice of assignment of creditor's rights jointly served by Nanmen ICBC and Huarong Fuzhou Office to the Preparatory Office stated that Nanmen ICBC assigned the principal debt and secured debt that had not yet been performed "as of June 20, 2000", with the total assigned amount being RMB 46,530,159.17. The creditor's rights subsequently assigned by the respondent Jiasheng Company from Huarong Fuzhou Office should not exceed this scope. This fully demonstrates that the assignee Huarong Fuzhou Office only enjoyed creditor's rights of RMB 46,530,159.17 against the Preparatory Office, and the Preparatory Office was entitled to defend against Jiasheng Company's claims beyond that amount based on the above notice of assignment of creditor's rights and the relevant provisions of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. 2. The court of first instance improperly consolidated five separate lawsuits into one for acceptance and trial, which constituted procedural impropriety. 3. The judgment of first instance unfairly ordered the appellant Preparatory Office to bear all first-instance acceptance fees. In summary, the Preparatory Office requested this Court to revoke the part of the first-instance judgment's first item that stated "interest on the loan principal of RMB 35.5 million generated after the assignment of creditor's rights on June 21, 2000 shall be paid at 0.21‰ per day until the date of actual repayment", and to dismiss Jiasheng Company's corresponding claim; and to order Jiasheng Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The respondent Jiasheng Company argued in its defense: 1. The creditor's rights transferred from Fujian ICBC to Huarong Fuzhou Office on June 21, 2000 already included interest after June 20, 2000, and the finding of the first-instance judgment was correct. (1) According to the provisions of Articles 1, 2, and 3 of the Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement No. 1-2-2-2-2010 signed between Fujian ICBC and Huarong Fuzhou Office on June 21, 2000, after the assignment, "Huarong replaces ICBC as the creditor under the loan contracts and enjoys the corresponding creditor's rights under the loan contracts." Therefore, the interest after June 20, 2000 accrued to the new creditor, Huarong Fuzhou Office. (2) According to the Notice of Assignment of Creditor's Rights (2000) Rong Gong Zheng Nei Min Zi No. 8299 notarized by the Fuzhou Notary Public Office, Fujian ICBC and Huarong Fuzhou Office had unequivocally informed the Preparatory Office in the above notice that "our branch decides to assign to Huarong Fuzhou Office the principal debt and secured debt that have not yet been performed by the borrower and guarantor as of June 20, 2000, i.e., our branch's loan principal debt and secured debt, and has signed the Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement No. 1-2-2-2-2010." The above notice clearly stated that the entire loan principal debt and secured debt had been assigned to Huarong Fuzhou Office. (3) On December 8, 2000, Fujian ICBC and Huarong Fuzhou Office published a notice of assignment of creditor's rights on page B2 of Fujian Daily, again informing the Preparatory Office: "Fujian Branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and its sub-branches have lawfully assigned the loan principal debts and corresponding accessory rights of the following enterprises to the Fuzhou Office of China Huarong Asset Management Corporation." (4) According to Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving the Acquisition, Management, and Disposal of Non-performing Assets of State-owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies: "If the debtor defaults on a loan, and the method for calculating interest agreed in the original loan contract does not violate laws or regulations, that agreement is effective. If there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, interest and compound interest shall be calculated in accordance with the People's Bank of China's Rules on the Management of RMB Interest Rates." Under this judicial interpretation, after the assignment of creditor's rights to Huarong Fuzhou Office, Huarong Fuzhou Office had the right to collect interest after June 20, 2000 from the Preparatory Office according to the original contract. (5) According to the principle of principal and accessory debts, when the principal debt is assigned, interest as an accessory debt is also assigned. 2. This case is a lawsuit arising from the same fact of assignment of creditor's rights and should be consolidated. 3. The first-instance judgment correctly ordered the Preparatory Office to bear all first-instance acceptance fees. In summary, Jiasheng Company requested this Court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

In the second instance, in addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, this Court further found: On November 29, 2004, Huarong Fuzhou Office issued a Certification of Assignment of Creditor's Rights to the court of first instance, stating: "...the principal of the creditor's rights under the above contracts is RMB 35.5 million, and the interest (temporarily calculated as of September 21, 2004) is RMB 28,746,682.79. The assigned principal and interest total RMB 64,246,682.79. The interest from September 22, 2004 is also assigned."

Opinion of the Court: The parties to this case have no dispute concerning the principal debt of RMB 35,500,000 and the interest accrued up to June 20, 2000, amounting to RMB 11,030,159.17, as confirmed in the two debt assignment agreements. Accordingly, this Court affirms the part of the first item of the original judgment relating to such amounts. The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the Preparatory Office should be obligated to pay the interest accrued after June 21, 2000.

First, as stipulated in the debt assignment contracts, when the Huarong Fuzhou Office acquired the unsatisfied claims under the five loan contracts and three guarantee contracts from the Fujian Branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China on June 20, 2000, it did not expressly waive the interest claims arising after the assignment. On November 29, 2004, when Jiasheng Company obtained the same claims through assignment from the Huarong Fuzhou Office, it also did not expressly waive the corresponding interest claims.

Second, the "corresponding interest" without a specific amount stated in the several "Notices of Payment Demand" issued by the Huarong Fuzhou Office to the Preparatory Office, and the statement in the "Certificate of Debt Assignment" issued by the Huarong Fuzhou Office to the original trial court on November 29, 2004, to the effect that "the principal of the claim is RMB 35,500,000, and the interest (provisionally calculated up to September 21, 2004), together with the interest accruing from September 22, 2004, shall be assigned accordingly," also indicate that the Huarong Fuzhou Office never waived the interest claims after June 21, 2000.

Furthermore, bank interest is the return on the principal claim and constitutes statutory fruits. Unless otherwise specifically provided by law or specially agreed by the parties, the right to claim fruits transfers simultaneously with the transfer of ownership of the principal property.

Although the claims in this case have been assigned twice, the contracting parties did not expressly indicate any waiver of the interest after the assignment. Therefore, the original judgment ordering the debtor, the Preparatory Office, to repay the creditor, Jiasheng Company, the interest from June 21, 2000, until the date of payment is not improper, and this Court should affirm it. However, the calculation standard should be made in stages according to the People's Bank of China's overdue loan interest rate for the corresponding periods. The original judgment uniformly applied a daily rate of 0.00021 without considering the changes in the People's Bank of China's overdue loan interest rate, and this Court corrects this.

Regarding the issue of consolidation of trials in this case, this Court holds that this case is a lawsuit arising from the assignment of claims. Jiasheng Company filed the lawsuit against the same debtor based on the same debt assignment contract and the same legal relationship. Therefore, there is no issue of consolidation of trials.

In summary, the original judgment found the facts clearly. Except for the improper expression of the calculation standard for overdue penalty interest, which should be adjusted, the application of law in the other aspects is not improper, and this Court affirms it. The appeal grounds of the appellant, the Preparatory Office, are untenable, and this Court does not support them. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraphs (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders judgment as follows:

1. Affirm Items 2, 3, and 4 of the main text of Civil Judgment No. (2004) Min Chu Zi No. 67 of Fujian High People's Court;

2. Amend Item 1 of the main text of the original judgment as follows: Fuzhou Commercial Building Preparatory Office shall repay to Fujian Jiasheng Investment Co., Ltd. the loan principal of RMB 35,500,000, the interest of RMB 11,030,159.17, and overdue penalty interest (calculated in stages from June 21, 2000, until the date of actual payment according to the People's Bank of China's overdue loan interest rate for the corresponding periods).

The above amounts payable shall be paid within 10 days from the day following the service of this judgment. Late payment shall be handled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 267,710 shall be executed in accordance with the first-instance judgment; the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 267,710 shall be borne by the appellant, Fujian Commercial Building Preparatory Office.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Xu Ruibai

Acting Judge: Jia Wei

Acting Judge: Sha Ling

October 21, 2005

Court Clerk: Yuan Hongxia
